source_spans.locator: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published p.451, Abstract: three response-competition studies; relevant-processing load varied by set size or processing requirement; distractor interference found only under low load

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published pp.452-453, load hypothesis: limited perceptual capacity, spare-capacity allocation to irrelevant stimuli under low load, and explicit caveat that the load effect need not be a sharp threshold

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published p.454, General Method / Operationalizing Perceptual Load: Eriksen response-competition procedure, three load manipulations, and incompatible-versus-neutral interference as the primary measure of irrelevant distractor processing

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published pp.456-457, Experiment 1 results and summary: incompatible-distractor interference significant under low set-size load and absent under high set-size load; conclusion independent of target-distractor separation and overall RT

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published pp.462-464, Experiment 3 results and General Discussion: interference significant only in the low-load detection task; convergence across three load manipulations; load associated with distractor interference rather than overall RT alone

Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance 21(3), published pp.464-465, Nature of Capacity Limits and elimination-of-interference discussion: general capacity-limit account, reduced irrelevant processing with greater load, unresolved general-versus-specific resource architecture

provenance.venue: Journal of Experimental Psychology: Human Perception and Performance

conditions: focused-attention response-competition tasks in which target-relevant perceptual processing demand is experimentally varied while a physically distinct irrelevant distractor is present
population: undergraduate participants drawn from University of California, Berkeley and Tel-Aviv University pools across Experiments 1-3
task: choice response to target identity while relevant processing load is manipulated by display set size, feature-versus-conjunction processing, or detection-versus-identification requirements and distractor compatibility is varied

nodes.description: experimentally varied target-relevant perceptual processing demand, operationalized by set size or processing requirements
physically distinct task-irrelevant distractor whose identity is incompatible, neutral, or compatible with the target response
latency of the required target response
incompatible-versus-neutral target reaction-time difference used as the primary interference index
Eriksen-style response-competition procedure varying relevant-processing demand and distractor compatibility
general limited perceptual-capacity structure invoked by the source; the paper leaves general versus specific-resource implementation unresolved
processing or identification of the task-irrelevant distractor inferred from incompatible-distractor interference

relations.description: target response time varies with the experimentally manipulated relevant-processing demand and the response relation of the irrelevant distractor
incompatible-distractor interference is present under lower relevant-processing demand and is strongly reduced or absent under higher demand across the tested manipulations
the source uses incompatible-versus-neutral response interference as evidence for identification or processing of the irrelevant distractor
under the source's capacity account, greater demand from relevant processing leaves less or no spare perceptual capacity for irrelevant processing; the exact resource architecture is left unresolved
the response-competition procedure supplies the incompatible-versus-neutral reaction-time interference measure
